title: Engineer-first QuickShot: Rapid Battle Brief (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a short, engineer-centric battle brief for rapid pilot conversations and SE enablement. Build a 6-slide QuickShot that helps sellers jump into technical discovery with minimal prep, shows predictable economic levers, and provides an operations-safe fallback plan.

Audience:
- Sales Engineers and Platform Sellers doing 20–40 minute discovery/demos for product teams and platform engineers.
- Secondary: Solutions Engineers running quick pilots for midmarket customers.

One-line thesis:
Make the first 15 minutes high-confidence: get to measurable SLO targets, a pilot scope, and a fallback policy.

Slide skeleton (6 slides, 3–5 bullets each):
1) 30s opener + value hypothesis
   - Opening: "Reduce inference unpredictability — latency, cost, reliability — so engineering teams can ship features."
   - Quick value hypothesis tailored to target persona (Platform Engineer vs Product Team).
   - Micro-ask: run a short 1-week pilot with clear success metrics.

2) Where teams get stuck (engineer pain signals)
   - Bursty traffic kills token economics and SLOs.
   - Model regressions and rollouts without observability.
   - Vendor lock-in + noisy capacity planning.
   - Callouts we should check for during discovery (prefix length, concurrency expectations, data residency).

3) Redwood QuickShot pattern (how we help)
   - Pin model version + staged rollout (canary > ramp).
   - Predictable throughput with Dedicated pools and autoscale knobs.
   - Caching and KV prefix suggestions to cut token counts by 30–70% in many UIs.
   - Fallbacks: lower-precision model / regional spillover / circuit-breaker policies.

4) Pilot plan (week-by-week)
   - Day 0–1: Instrument endpoints, sample traces, establish baseline latency/95/99, token mix.
   - Day 2–4: Apply batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendation for dev environment.
   - Day 5–7: Run 1–2 traffic windows (synthetic + real) to validate SLOs and cost estimates.
   - Success criteria (pick 1 primary): p95 < X ms OR cost per 1k tokens < $Y OR deterministic throughput = N rps.

5) Objection plays (engineer + procurement)
   - "We can host ourselves": talk opportunity cost, kernel/ops complexity, and our dedicated autoscale testing.
   - "Latency spikes": point to prefix/KV caching + regional routing and show historical p95 improvements.
   - "Cost unpredictability": demo token breakdown, batch/caching toggles, reserved cap options.
   - "Compliance/GDPR": map private deploy options and KMS/HSM story; offer an architecture whiteboard session.

6) Rapid demo script & fallback checklist
   - Demo script (6 min): topology > baseline call to API > show trace with KV hit > flip batching > show cost delta.
   - Fallback checklist for pilot-run: compatible model fallback, regional spillover engaged, and a throttling policy with circuit-breaker thresholds.

Speaker notes / tactical cues:
- If customer mentions "real-time" or "sub-second": ask about typical sequence lengths and concurrency spikes; recommend Dedicated + small-batch policy.
- If they mention "production security": surface Private deployment timeline (usually 6–12 weeks for on-prem), short-term hosted mitigations (VPC peering + KMS).
- Use the phrase "predictable SLOs" not just "low latency" — sellers find that framing easier to operationalize with customers.

Sample customer scenario (short vignette):
- Fintech company with 200k monthly active users, chat flow average 350 tokens, occasional spikes to 200 concurrent calls. Current p95 = 1.2s, cost = $0.015/token. Pilot target: p95 < 600ms during normal load and cost per session down 25% with caching.
- Recommended Pilot: model v1.3 quantized, cache common prompts, reserved capacity at 2x baseline bursts.

Metrics & what to instrument during pilot:
- Latency (p50/p95/p99), Token mix (prompt vs completion), Cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit rate, Throughput (rps) per GPU, Model-side errors + fallback triggers.

Quick technical checklist for SE before call:
- Confirm API key + IP allowlist done.
- Have sample trace or logs to upload (or request customer trace collection).
- Have 2 synthetic workloads (steady & spike) prepped in Postman or loader.

Playbook experiments to try (A/B inside Pilot):
- Toggle aggressive batching vs latency-first mode to show cost/latency tradeoffs live.
- Apply prefix-caching only on top 10 intents to show incremental return.
- Run quantized model variant to show cost delta and confirm no quality regression on defined evals.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get benchmark artifacts from 'serving-runtime' team for quantized v1.3 on T4 vs A10. (owner: Ravi)
- Wire up an internal trace dashboard tile for the demo (owner: Maya).
- Draft a one-page pilot SOW with reserved capacity options + cancellation windows (owner: Liam).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Pilot looks good in synthetic tests but regresses under unpredictable user inputs. Mitigation: keep a quality-monitoring cohort and rollback rule in the rollout policy.
- Risk: Procurement delays. Mitigation: offer a short-term hosted contract with clear exit and data handling terms.

Appendix (quick notes for SEs):
- Example curl call to show (one-liner) and what to look for in response headers: x-rw-latency, x-rw-cache-hit.
- Short prompt optimization checklist (reduce repetition, canonicalize user context, limit system messages).

Suggested next steps before sharing to field: 
- Convert slide skeleton into a 6-slide deck and run one dry run with two SEs.
- Attach a one-page pilot SOW template and the sample synthetic workload scripts.
- Validate the quantized benchmark numbers with Applied ML team and embed into slide 4.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Need a snappy 15s opener video clip (screen capture) showing the delta in dashboard after flipping batching.
- Consider an alternate 4-slide variant for executive-level meetings focused on cost & compliance only.

End of brief.

(Working doc — feel free to copy/iterate. Keep versioning in GitHub sales-decks.)
